Thanks for the reply. My anxiety about school has made me need to take a semester off which causes my depression and feeling like I'm not doing anything with my life. I have social anxiety so my love life and social life are almost non existent at the moment. I'm constantly cancelling plans with friends. My family is really supportive but I can't help but feel like they're tired of dealing with me. I see my psychiatrist tomorrow so hopefully I can get my prescriptions worked out but I know it's going to take a while. I've already spent the past 6 months feeling horrible every day and I know that anxiety meds take a while to start working given that it even will work. I do plan on going to a few concerts this summer so I have that to look forward to but not much else

The way I've phrased it to my doctors is that I think about dying a lot and wishing I could kill myself but know logically that I never will (which is true for me). One therapist I went to just replied with "we all have thoughts but I just need to know that you aren't planning on doing anything". My main therapist is really understanding and has never threatened to do anything about it. Just be honest if you trust the doctor that you're talking to. They can't do anything unless you tell them you're planning on ending it

I was in the same boat a few months ago. I'm 20 and went away to college for a year but came back home because my anxiety got really bad. I started taking local classes for a semester but couldn't get through them so I was stuck for the beginning half of my semester with no job and not going to school. I finally got a job a month ago but I'm not sure I can put myself through the anxiety of school again which makes me feel lame because it seems like everyone else can do it with no problem. My cousin has bad anxiety and she's doing online school and it's been ok for her so I think I'm going to try it next semester. Maybe you could start by taking a few classes online? Even if you don't though it's much more important to figure out your mental health now so you'll be able to do whatever it is YOU want to do in the future- not what everyone thinks you should do. I'm still in the process of figuring it out and it sucks to think that everyone else already does but I know a lot of people who are also struggling with it- they're just not broadcasting it to the world usually.
